The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed
Why, in plain words: Turning on a new monthly-spending feature made the shop's account pages run a calculation that tried to divide by zero, so those pages failed.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 1s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,422.30 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- demo user: resolved it from the Argus UI - "kept the flag off and told the checkout team"
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - not judged by Argus (demo user resolved it first), still in place

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 14, 2026, 11:40 to 11:48:01 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 4 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 14, 2026, 12:06:27 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 14, 2026, 11:46:55 UTC
Ended by: demo user from the Argus UI, Nov 14, 2026, 11:48:01 UTC - kept the flag off and told the checkout team

Summary
The service broke at 11:40 UTC. demo user reported the incident resolved at 11:48:01 UTC, 8 minutes 1 second later. 27.2% of requests failed while it was broken, against 0.9% before it began. At its worst, 40.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 5,422.30 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Turning on a new monthly-spending feature made the shop's account pages run a calculation that tried to divide by zero, so those pages failed. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - not judged, still in place. If monthly-spend-feature is switched on again, account page requests could fail again with the same division by zero.

Impact
8m 1s - onset until reported resolved
40.5% - peak error rate
2,940 - requests failed
0.9% to 27.2% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
5,422.30 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
Switching monthly-spend-feature on sent account page requests through the spend-summary code, which divided by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and failed the request with a ZeroDivisionError. The record does not show why the divisor was zero on these requests.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, well above the usual low level of failures.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 occurrences in 37 minutes, 11:10–11:46; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 11:43
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 11:40–11:46
why 1 Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors were logged over 11:40–11:46 UTC and were not seen in the log window before the onset.
  Evidence:
    G5309
    G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 36 occurrences in 30 minutes, 11:10–11:39
why 2 The spend-summary code ran because admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at 11:40:31 UTC. Flag evaluations were split between off and on in 11:40 UTC and were all on over 11:41–11:46 UTC. Before that, the flag was off over 11:10–11:39 UTC.
  Evidence:
    P1 11:40:31 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 / on 99 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 11:40
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 11:41–11:46
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 11:10–11:39
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 14 11:41; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change.
      T7
      T8
    A rollout still under way: the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name.
      T9
    The ClientDisconnected account page errors: they were already logged before the onset, over 11:10–11:39 UTC, while account pages otherwise rendered normally.
      G46bc
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 occurrences in 26 minutes, 11:11–11:36
why 3 The flag change broke account pages because the spend-summary path it turned on divides by a value that was zero on these requests.
  Evidence:
    G5309
Contributing factors
- The flag change reached all account page traffic in a single step. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on a rising error rate were seen for monthly-spend-feature. (AI-2)
- No test or pre-production check of the spend-summary path was seen before the flag was switched on in production. (AI-3)
- The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to on-call paging, so nobody was paged when it fired. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 11:40:31 UTC. The newly enabled spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% to 20-40%. | 0.93 | tried, not judged

Trigger
Suspected, not confirmed: monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 11:40:31 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
Resolved by demo user from the Argus UI, 11:48:01 UTC - kept the flag off and told the checkout team
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 11:47:36 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | not judged, still in place

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 11:40 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 11:46:29 UTC, 6 minutes 29 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so a zero divisor cannot fail the account page, and add a test for that case, before monthly-spend-feature is switched on again. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-2 | Roll out monthly-spend-feature, and flags like it, in percentage stages that stop automatically when the service's error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Require that the code path behind a feature flag passes tests on production-like data in a pre-production environment before the flag can be switched on in production. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Route the HighErrorRate alert for io-shop to the on-call paging rotation. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 58 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 1 minute 7 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)

Response effort
none - engineer time
105,758 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/9ba2837d-2a18-46b2-aa67-f7372d4ed7aa
Changes to production read

Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 11:10–11:39

Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-13
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
✗ Root-cause analysis complete (not met)
  no candidate was confirmed
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, account pages failed for shoppers who opened them for {duration}. Turning on a new monthly-spending feature made those pages run a calculation that tried to divide by zero. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. Argus estimates the incident cost the shop {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so no on-call responder was called in. To end it, Argus reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature, and that change is still in place. A demo user then closed the incident from the Argus UI before Argus had judged whether the revert worked. The demo user noted that they had kept the flag off and told the checkout team.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
